subject: Observability add-ons — dashboard ingestion rate, trace sampling & credit path
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel@nh-health.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Question on observability add-ons pricing and onboarding credits

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the dashboards and trace views look great. Before we move a formal PO through procurement, two quick items procurement flagged:

1) We expect a large initial ingestion spike during onboarding (around 350TB of trace/span data across a two-week migration window). Are there temporary surge credits or a one-time ingestion uplift to avoid overage charges?
2) For advanced dashboards, we wanted clarity on the default sample rate and whether you can offer a pilot-level sample-rate override (higher retention for the first 30 days) and any associated crediting.

If you can sketch options and a rough crediting schedule, procurement will be able to align on numbers. Attaching our projected ingestion CSV as a sample.

—Sam
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel@nh-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on observability add-ons pricing and onboarding credits

Hi Sam — great to hear the team liked the demo. Pushed this to our pricing ops folks but wanted to outline two pragmatic paths so Procurement has something to review quickly:

Option A — One-time surge credit
- We grant a one-time ingestion credit equal to 80% of the projected onboarding delta (applies to trace ingestion only), capped at a configurable dollar amount.
- Credit is applied to the first invoice after onboarding and will be visible as a line item.

Option B — 60-day elevated sample-rate pilot
- Increase trace sample retention and dashboard ingestion for 60 days at no additional charge; consumption above the committed baseline is covered by a phased credit (40% first 30 days, 20% next 30 days).
- Intended to give engineering time to smooth the migration and tune sampling.

Both options require a short SOW amendment and sign-off from Procurement (I can draft). Attaching the baseline pricing sheet and a template SOW. Looping in Kimberly for the formal crediting language and Jordan on dashboard seat/ingestion rates.

Regards,
Marcus
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on observability add-ons pricing and onboarding credits

Marcus / Jordan — draft language below we can push to Procurement. I made the crediting explicit and added measurable triggers so finance can model it: 

Draft credit schedule (preferred)
- Onboarding surge credit: 75% credit applied to onboarding ingestion delta (Delta = observed onboarding ingestion over baseline committed ingestion for first 14 days). Credit applied as a dollar value and amortized across first two invoices.
- Pilot sample-rate taper: 30-day elevated retention window (we recommend 60 days only for very large migrations; 30 days is our standard). Crediting: 50% credit for the first 15 days of elevated retention, 25% credit for days 16–30.
- Dashboard ingestion uplift: For dashboard heavy queries (dashboard tile refreshes that hit raw ingest), we offer a 45-day waiver on query egress credits up to a 2x baseline query rate.

Requirements:
- Customer provides a migration runbook and expected spike window at least 5 business days in advance; engineering will enable surge protection.
- Any usage above the uplift caps billed at standard rates.

I'll attach the SOW with this language and the sample ingestion report Marcus received. Jordan — confirm the dashboard tile refresh definition and whether we should tie the uplift to API key or project ID.

-Kim
Director, Commercial Pricing
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel@nh-health.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <contracts@nh-health.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on observability add-ons pricing and onboarding credits

Thanks Marcus and Kim — that language is helpful. Procurement asked for two clarifications before we sign:

1) How do you verify the "onboarding ingestion delta"? If we provide the projected CSV, will Redwood accept it as the basis, or do you compute the delta from observed ingestion?
2) For the dashboard uplift, can the 45-day waiver be scoped to a named project so we don't accidentally absorb other teams' queries?

We're okay with the 30-day pilot if the crediting schedule above is explicit in the SOW and the SOW includes a one-paragraph runbook requirement. Attaching updated ingestion projections and a redline request to the SOW (SOW_NimbusHealth_Observability_v2.pdf).

—Sam
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <samuel@nh-health.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on observability add-ons pricing and onboarding credits

Sam — quick replies inline: 

1) Verification: we compute the delta from observed ingestion metrics during the 14-day onboarding window and reconcile against your projected CSV. We accept the CSV as the expected pattern but final credit is based on observed delta; reconciliation happens in the first invoice cycle. We will supply the reconciliation report (ingestion_sample_report.csv) as evidence.

2) Scoped uplift: yes — we will scope the 45-day dashboard query waiver to the project ID you specify in the SOW. Engineering will gate the uplift by API key/project tag.

I'll update the SOW with the verification paragraph and the scoped-waiver wording. Once you sign the attached SOW and Procurement returns the PO, we'll stage the onboarding and provision the elevated sample-rate window. I'll also put the DocuSign link in the updated SOW.

Next steps: Marcus to receive signed SOW/PO; Kimberly to approve final credit line amounts; Grace to schedule the migration kick-off with Customer Engineering.

Thanks — Jordan
Senior Product GTM, Redwood Inference
